articles.title: Bloom Energy Stock Is Sliding: What's Driving The Move?
articles.teaser: Bloom Energy Corp shares are trading lower Friday as traders take profits after AI-power run, with S&P 500 up 0.2% and Industrials down 0.4%.
articles.body:
Bloom Energy Corp (NYSE:BE) shares are trading lower on Friday as traders digest a fast run tied to the AI data-center power-demand theme and lean into profit-taking during a mixed tape where the S&P 500 is up 0.2% but Industrials are down 0.4%.

  • Bloom Energy shares are sliding. Why is BE stock dropping?

What Is Bloom Energy’s New Agreement With Nebius?

Bloom recently struck a 10-year, multi-phase "behind-the-meter" agreement with Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) that could generate up to $2.6 billion in total service fees, built around on-site power generation for new AI infrastructure. Nebius expects the first project to be operational this year and sized at 328 megawatts of installed capacity.

Bloom's rally setup has also been tied to the idea that the AI bottleneck is electricity, not GPUs, after grid connections, substations and permitting delays pushed some large builds toward 2030.

Bloom Energy Stock: Key Levels To Watch

The bigger-picture trend is still pointed up: the stock is up 1373.18% over the past 12 months and remains above its 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day moving averages, even after Friday's drop. The 50-day SMA is $221.10, and the 200-day SMA is $136.99, which highlights how extended the longer-term move has been.

Near-term, the stock is now trading 3.9% below its 20-day SMA ($284.78), a common spot where strong trends either reset and bounce or start a deeper mean reversion. The key "trend health" tell is whether buyers can defend prior breakout areas rather than letting price slide back into the earlier range.

Momentum is the more two-sided part of the setup right now: MACD is below its signal line and the histogram is negative, which points to upside pressure fading versus the prior upswing. In plain terms, MACD compares faster and slower trend signals—when it's below the signal line, it often means buyers need to re-accelerate to keep the rally pushing.

  • Key Resistance: $303.00 — a nearby round-number/pivot area where rebounds can stall after a sharp pullback
  • Key Support: $249.00 — a prior demand zone that sits near the current pullback path if selling continues

What Does Bloom Energy Do?

Bloom Energy designs, manufactures, sells and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems for on-site power generation. Its Bloom Energy Servers are fuel-flexible and can use natural gas, biogas and hydrogen to create 24/7 electricity for stationary applications, with sales in the United States and internationally.

That matters right now because "behind-the-meter" power is being pitched as a practical workaround when grid connections and permitting slow down large data-center builds.

Bloom Energy Benzinga Edge Scorecard Overview

Below is the Benzinga Edge scorecard for Bloom Energy, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses compared to the broader market:

  • Momentum: Bullish (Score: 99.73) — Even with today's dip, the stock is still behaving like a leader on a multi-month basis.
  • Value: Weak (Score: 0.64) — The market is pricing in a lot of upside, which can make pullbacks sharper when sentiment cools.
  • Growth: Bullish (Score: 98.59) — Expectations remain geared toward strong expansion, which helps explain the premium-style trading.

The Verdict: Bloom Energy’s Benzinga Edge signal reveals a classic High-Flyer setup, with momentum and growth doing most of the heavy lifting while value remains the clear weak spot. For longer-term bulls, that usually means trend support levels matter more than "cheapness," because breaks of key supports can unwind crowded positioning quickly.

Bloom Energy Stock Price Movement On Friday

BE Stock Price Activity: Bloom Energy shares were down 4.00% at $278.42 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Bloom and Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) recently struck a 10-year, multi-phase "behind-the-meter" agreement that could generate up to $2.6 billion in total service fees, built around on-site power generation for new AI infrastructure. Nebius expects the first project to be operational this year and sized at 328 megawatts of installed capacity.

That "deployable now" pitch is resonating because some massive 1-gigawatt AI campus builds are getting pushed out as far as 2030, keeping urgency on near-term power solutions.

With grid connections and permitting delaying large projects, Bloom's behind-the-meter model is being treated as a way to bypass those bottlenecks.

How Bloom Energy Generates On-Site Power

Bloom Energy designs, manufactures, sells and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems for on-site power generation. Its Bloom Energy Servers are fuel-flexible and can use natural gas, biogas, and hydrogen to produce 24/7 electricity for stationary applications, with sales in the U.S. and internationally.

That business model lines up cleanly with the current AI infrastructure problem: data centers need reliable power quickly, and "behind-the-meter" generation can reduce dependence on slow grid buildouts. The Nebius partnership highlights how Bloom's deployments can be positioned as a faster path to capacity when traditional utility timelines are stretched.

articles.title: Why Nebius Stock Is Surging On Thursday?
articles.teaser: Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) stock jumps Thursday following a SEC Schedule 13G filing revealing a $2.6B passive stake by Situational Awareness LP.
articles.body:
Shares of Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) are rallying sharply during Thursday’s trading session. The upward price action follows a major regulatory filing revealing significant institutional backing from a prominent artificial intelligence insider.

According to a Schedule 13G filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), hedge fund Situational Awareness LP disclosed a 5.6% passive stake in Nebius Group. The fund, managed by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner alongside co-portfolio manager Carl Shulman, reported holding 12,410,060 Class A ordinary shares.

Based on current market valuations, this position is worth approximately $2.6 billion. The event requiring the filing occurred on May 19, with the document officially signed and credited on Wednesday.

Aggressive AI Infrastructure Bets

The multi-billion-dollar investment aligns with Aschenbrenner's public thesis on the aggressive scaling of AI infrastructure.

In his research series Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead, Aschenbrenner emphasized that “American big business is gearing up to pour trillions of dollars into a long-unseen mobilization of American industrial might.”

His fund’s position in Nebius underscores a calculated bet on companies supporting the upcoming “trillion-dollar cluster” era of compute and data center expansion.

Fueling The Short Squeeze

Data from the latest reporting period shows that short interest in Nebius Group increased from 43.14 million to 45.10 million shares. This short exposure represents 21.1% of the company’s publicly available float.

With an average daily volume of 19.60 million shares, short sellers face a days-to-cover metric of 2.3 days.

What Is Nebius Group and Its Business Model?

Nebius is a vertically integrated cloud provider focusing on AI and high-performance computing. It is a carve-out of the previous Russian tech firm Yandex, following the Russian sanctions since the Ukraine-Russia war.

Nebius designs and operates its own data centers and servers across Europe and the US, with a total capacity of several hundred megawatts. In September, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) became a major Nebius client under a multiyear $17 billion revenue agreement to provide computing capacity.

NBIS Stock Price Activity: Nebius Group shares were up 8.33% at $225.73 at the time of publication on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro data.
